practices.practice: Create one MongoClient and reuse it (singleton pattern) instead of constructing a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Configure connection pooling and timeouts in the MongoDB driver (set reasonable maxPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) to avoid exhausting sockets and to ensure fast failover.

practices.practice: Always enforce TLS on connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Always connect with TLS/SSL enforced (e.g., mongodb+srv or tls=true in the connection string) and verify server certificates; disallow insecure connections in production.

practices.practice: Store connection information and credentials outside source code: keep connection strings out of repos, prefer environment variables or secret backends for local dev, and avoid printing or logging connection URIs.
practices.prior_belief: Do not commit the DocumentDB connection string or primary key to source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any keys) from environment variables or a secrets store at runtime.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Spring Data MongoDB to Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string security 'do not commit' quickstart

practices.practice: For serverless environments initialize the client outside the request handler and tune pool settings for short-lived invocations (low maxPoolSize, minPoolSize=0, small maxIdleTimeMS).

For long-running OLTP servers tune maxPoolSize/minPoolSize/connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS to match concurrency and fail-fast expectations (examples: maxPoolSize 50+, minPoolSize 10–20, connectTimeoutMS 5–10s).
Enable driver retryable reads and implement application-level exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors; avoid blind retries of non-idempotent writes.
practices.prior_belief: Enable and implement exponential backoff with jitter for retrying transient network and server selection errors, and make retries idempotent-aware (do not retry non-idempotent writes blindly).

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB maps MongoDB writeConcern/readConcern to the service consistency model and the account's consistency settings; client-specified writeConcern may be ignored, so use and document the account-level consistency configuration rather than relying on driver writeConcern to enforce durability.
practices.prior_belief: Set appropriate write concern and read concern for your risk-review workload (e.g., majority or w=1 depending on durability vs latency needs) and document this in configuration.
practices.source_name: Consistency levels for Azure Cosmos DB and the API for MongoDB

practices.practice: Create full-text search indexes with createSearchIndexes and query them via the $search aggregation stage (prefer createSearchIndexes + $search over the community $text operator).

When creating a server-side vector index, pick the appropriate kind (vector-diskann, vector-hnsw, vector-ivf), explicitly set dimensions and similarity (COS/L2/IP), and tune algorithm parameters (efConstruction/efSearch/m/numLists) for dataset size and latency needs.
practices.prior_belief: When creating the server-side vector index, explicitly set the index type (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN) and metric (cosine or euclidean/L2) to match the embedding model and tune parameters (efConstruction, M, nlist, etc.) for the dataset size and latency needs.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings consistently when using cosine (unit L2-normalize at ingest and query time) and store embedding metadata (model name, dimensions, embeddingVersion) alongside vectors.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize embeddings consistently (unit-normalize for cosine similarity or leave raw for L2) before storage and before query-time embedding generation so distance metrics behave predictably.

practices.practice: Store vectors as numeric arrays (number[]) with a fixed dimensionality that matches the index configuration; ensure the stored type is numeric and all documents use the same length.
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array field and record the embedding dimension in the document; ensure all stored embeddings across collections have identical dimensionality to the index configuration.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use the $search aggregation stage with the cosmosSearch operator for vector queries (vector, path, k), project the similarity score via {$meta: 'searchScore'}, and cap results with $limit / TOP N to control RU and latency.
practices.prior_belief: Limit and paginate search results (e.g., topK + offset or cursor) and enforce a max result size in the /review API to avoid expensive large scans and to make risk narratives deterministic.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Create additional single-field or compound indexes on frequently filtered metadata (e.g., bank_id, last_reviewed, risk_score) and keep a modest index budget per collection (review unused indexes).
practices.prior_belief: Create additional non-vector indexes on frequently queried fields (e.g., bank_id, sanction_list_id, last_reviewed, risk_score) and use compound or partial indexes where appropriate to speed metadata filtering before vector search.

practices.practice: Use projection to return only required fields (do not return embeddings or large text fields unless explicitly needed) to reduce network transfer and memory pressure in API responses.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection to return only required fields (avoid returning full text and embeddings when not needed) to reduce network transfer and memory pressure in review API responses.

practices.practice: For bulk seeding/writes, use unordered/batched inserts (ordered:false), tune batch size (~<=1000 per batch) and parallelism, and avoid large multi-document transactions for high-throughput seed workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid expensive multi-document transactions for high-throughput vector inserts; batch writes and use ordered=false with retries for bulk seeding, and verify idempotency of seed scripts.

practices.practice: Use JSON schema validation (collection validators) or application-level checks and include a schemaVersion field to support schema evolution and fail-fast ingestion of malformed documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use schema validation (collection validators) or application-level validation for critical fields (embedding array length, required metadata, date format) and fail fast on malformed documents during seed or ingestion.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON limit and design large fields to live in side collections when they grow (the 16 MB maximum still applies).
practices.prior_belief: Model correspondent and source documents with a stable unique _id, include metadata fields (source, created_at, updated_at, text_snippet, embedding_dim), and keep document sizes well below the DB's max document size (avoid >16MB).

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (managed identity) + RBAC or least-privilege secondary users over long-lived admin passwords; rotate any secondary-user passwords and avoid embedding credentials in apps.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer using a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault) or managed identity to store and retrieve the cluster credentials instead of raw env vars when running in cloud or CI/CD.

practices.practice: Harden network access by using Private Endpoints or firewall allowlists and, where possible, disabling public network access to the cluster.
practices.prior_belief: Harden network access: restrict the cluster to known client IPs, use VNet private endpoints if available, and avoid exposing the DB's primary key to browsers or client-side code.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostics and slow-query / search logs, centralize them in Log Analytics or similar, and alert on connection errors, slow queries, vector-index health, RU/throughput, and CPU/memory saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Implement monitoring and alerting on connection errors, slow queries, vector index health, and RU/throughput or CPU/memory metrics; enable driver command monitoring or Azure diagnostic logs as available.

practices.practice: Pick a shard/partition key based on query and write patterns (e.g., hashed bank_id for writes or date-based for time-partitioned workloads) and validate distribution to avoid hot partitions.
practices.prior_belief: For high-cardinality or growing datasets, choose an appropriate shard key (or partition key) based on query patterns (e.g., hash(bank_id) or reviewed_date) and test distribution to avoid hot partitions.

practices.practice: When changing vector index parameters or reindexing (especially HNSW/DiskANN), perform the operation in a maintenance window and validate on a small subset first because large builds can exhaust memory or affect performance.
practices.prior_belief: Index maintenance: when changing vector index parameters or reindexing, perform it during a maintenance window and re-seed a small subset first to measure impact on latency and storage.

practices.practice: Use the search index's custom analyzers and operators (fuzzy, phrase with slop, edgeGram, pathHierarchy) to tune full-text matching and to build hybrid BM25+vector retrieval patterns when needed.
For local development using the DocumentDB gateway, use the recommended gateway port and TLS (gateway images expose MongoDB on port 10260 and require SCRAM-SHA-256 / TLS configuration).
Always supply k (topK) and tune efSearch/nProbes or equivalent query-time parameters to trade recall for latency when running vector searches.

practices.practice: Use stable unique _id values and include metadata fields (source, created_at, updated_at, embeddingDims, embeddingModel) in documents to support auditing and reindexing.
Protect PII by redacting or tokenizing sensitive fields before indexing/searching and store provenance metadata for traceability.
Prefer DiskANN for large production vector stores, HNSW for medium-scale (~50k) demos, and IVF for small datasets; scale index type to dataset size to balance memory and recall.
